gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the $169.99 Power Watchdog Gen II 30A (PWD30W) only lights red, shows an error code and sends an app alert when it detects a fault, while the Gen II 30A EPO version is the one that cuts power below 104 V or above 132 V and turns it back on after 90 s of stable power, even though both take the same replaceable surge module (RSM30W).
standout_why: I compared against the cited rvupgradestore PWD30EPOW page. It gives 2,300 J and the 104 V / 132 V cutoffs, but only for the EPO model. ChatGPT's own answer just says 'provides surge protection' for the $169.99 Gen II and 'automatic safety shutoff' for the EPO. No result explains that the non-EPO unit doesn't disconnect on low or high voltage. None shows that the extra $110–$210 for the EPO buys the shutoff relay and not a bigger surge rating, since one surge module fits both. None gives Southwire Surge Guard's 102 V low cutoff for comparison. I couldn't open the powerwatchdog.com pages ChatGPT cited (certificate error), so I couldn't check whether the maker states the difference there.
decides: For a whole-RV smart device, the cheaper Gen II PWD30W is a surge protector with a monitor and alerts: it doesn't disconnect the RV in a brownout or when voltage runs high. Shoppers who want automatic protection at the pedestal should get the PWD30EPOW (seen at $279.99 on sale, list $379.99) or another full-protection unit such as the Southwire Surge Guard 34931 (cuts out under 102 V). Low campground voltage is what damages AC compressors, so the shutoff is the feature that matters. Buy the PWD30W only if alerts are enough for you. The 15 A Kasa or Minoston plugs are only for single appliances inside the RV.
